summary:
The fix is proven. I found 7 Low findings and nothing at Medium or above, so none of them needs a push on its own.

Every planted bug failed where the table said it would. The fixed tree passed 1,220 runs with no failure. Each item below was checked against its log; the notes file has the full record.

| Claim | Proof | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| The loop runs the right binary and prints every failing test (C3) | u3c_held_loop.sh:32-33 and :39 stop with exit 2 unless the binary is npt_net-ed8673eeeaf4db12. Each failing test's whole stdout block is printed (p1.log:54 and :103). | The printed list of failing test names is cut off (TE-UH1-2) |
| L1 confirmed the cause | l1.log: 189 runs (188 exit 0, run 94 exit 101). Run 94: G-NC2 alone fails at :2302 (HEAD's :2300 plus D-1's 2 lines), [1, 0] against [0, 0]. Excess 14,326 B, first losses 28, over_waiting [1, 0] = held_over_bound, over_at_write [0, 0]. Every item of the plan's Confirmed line holds and no stop line is met. D-1's over_at_write is the same formula at the same place as the new check_held_bound(dir), so run 94 is also a direct positive control: where the old check fired, the new one counted 0. | none |
| The new checks raise no false failure | e3a.log: G-NC2 alone, 600 of 600, each "1 passed", writes above [0, 0], samples above [0, 0]. e3b.log: the stalled-client test, 600 of 600. e3c.log: the whole binary, 20 of 20, 169 passed. All three logs show tree hash a7199f7a and binary hash 2cf1e962. | E3 cannot show the old flake is gone (TE-UH1-3) |
| Each check still catches a real overflow | P1 to P5 in p1.log to p5.log: each plant has its own source and binary hash, and the first failing assert in each test matches the table. P1: stalled-client [1, 0] at :782. P2: G-NC2 [121, 0]. P3: [134, 0] and [1144, 0], both "held only falls". P4: [137, 129], plus G-NC2's hang guard at :2290. P5: [0, 172]. P1's G-NC2 failure [1, 0] is evidence under C3, not a stop. | P1's G-NC2 failure depends on timing (TE-UH1-4) |
| The plants were taken out again | The final tree hash a7199f7a is the same in e5.log, light.log and E3. Today's diff contains no plant. Each plant's failure pattern also rules out the one before it. | The in-between restores rest on unlogged sha256 checks (build.md:77-95) |
| The change is test-only | Every changed non-doc line is in a #[cfg(test)] item or statement (delay.rs Life struct cfg(test) at :377, then :523-524, :537-564, :634-635) or in delay_tests.rs. E5 rebuilt npt-net in release and npt-lab's hash is unchanged (98c3967e…). | none |
| The test counts stay 552 / 632 (C5) | No test was added: 169 passed and 12 ignored in the bites npt_net binary, before (l1.log) and after (e3c.log). "All 11 steps" matches the 11 steps in check.mjs:2614-2649. | The pass bar still has to be written in the notes before the call (build.md stops at 11:35). refs must be read just before the call, because each committed reviewer notes file adds a tracked file. |

The new checks cannot flake:
- **Growth sites:** the held bytes grow only at delay.rs:829→:830 and :1597→:1615, and no sample sits between the extend and the check.
- **Pending assert:** poll_write is Pending only when free ≤ 22 B (:1584-1595), so asking for a whole record is exactly as strict as the old 100 B write.

The plan for what comes next is right. If the fix pass edits a held_grew assert or its message, re-run P3, P4, E3a, E3b and the light check on that change.

The report must say four things:
- E3 shows only that the new checks never fail on a sound tree. That the old flake is gone rests on the code and on L1 run 94.
- P1's G-NC2 failure is a timing one; P1's deterministic catch is the stalled-client test.
- No plant moves an up-direction byte outside a write (P3 is down only). P4's up count of 129 shows the up branch of the between-writes check does count.
- The gate passes have no log yet.

findings.where: spikes/netcode-proof/crates/net/src/l2/delay_tests.rs:787, :2313 (the message); delay.rs:558-564 (check_held_falls); plan u3c-held-1-plan-draft.md:129 ("becomes a counted fact")
findings.what: The message "held only falls between writes" says more than the check tests. check_held_falls only counts a sample above what the latest write left; it does not check that the held bytes never rise. A growth outside model_write that follows an equal or larger drain would go uncounted. The bound claim itself still holds, since every sample is at most the latest write's held bytes, which check_held_bound held to the bound.
findings.fix: In the report and the card, state the counted fact as "no sample above what the latest write left". Follow-up for the advisor, since C1 fixed the message text: make the check strict by adding `self.life.held_at_write[d] = self.life.held_at_write[d].min(len)` after the comparison, and rename the field. P3 and P4 still catch it, and it adds no false failure, because no sample sits between the extend (:829, :1597) and model_write (:830, :1615).

findings.where: .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-held-1/u3c_held_loop.sh:70; .gate/u3c-held-1/p1.log:13-52 and p3.log:13-52 against p1-1-1.log:287-289 and p3-1-1.log:287-289
findings.what: The script's "libtest's failures list" takes every 4-space-indented line from the FIRST `failures:` line, which comes before the stdout blocks. With backtraces on, it picks up the backtrace "at ..." lines, and head -40 then cuts off the test names. The call logs of P1 and P3 hold 40 backtrace lines and neither failing test's name. The evidence still holds: the "2 failed" summary plus two whole stdout blocks, and the per-run logs list both names.
findings.fix: In the report, cite the per-run logs' lists (p1-1-1.log:287-289, p3-1-1.log:287-289) for "no other test failed". For reuse, print only the list after the LAST `failures:` line.

findings.what: E3 shows that the new checks raise no false failure. It does not show that the old one is gone. The old failure was only ever seen in whole-binary runs (1 in 189 here). E3a and E3b ran the tests one at a time, a mode never shown to reproduce it (L2 was not run). E3c's 20 whole-binary runs would catch a 1-in-100 failure only about 18 % of the time (1 - 0.99^20). By the rule of three, 0 failures bound the rate below 0.5 % in single-test mode and below 15 % for the whole binary, at 95 % confidence. That the transient is no longer counted rests on the code (the bound is checked only inside model_write, where admission guarantees it) and on L1 run 94, where D-1's over_at_write, the new formula, counted [0, 0].
findings.fix: The report states exactly this, citing l1.log:227 for the run-94 control. Never write "600 of 600 shows the flake is gone".

findings.where: .gate/u3c-held-1/p1.log:103-109 (G-NC2 writes above the bound [1, 0]); netcode-architect-design.md F15; test-engineer-evidence.md:61-67 (F11)
findings.what: Under P1, G-NC2 failed at "...at every write" with a count of 1. This is a timing-dependent catch: it needs a write while a released record is still waiting to be taken. It also disproves the premise in the design notes' F15 and my own F11 that S drains at once in G-NC2. C3 pre-rules the failure as evidence, so this is not a stop.
findings.fix: The report counts only the stalled-client test (p1.log:56-59, [1, 0], deterministic) as P1's proof. It records G-NC2's failure as a timing catch, and notes that the premise is corrected: released records do sometimes wait untaken at G-NC2's writes.

findings.what: Both GATE PASS results (09:53 and 11:34 UTC) are recorded with no log, while every other evidence item has its log under .gate/u3c-held-1/.
findings.fix: When step 8 runs the gate on the commit, keep its output in a form that needs no approval, or quote its PASS summary line with the time in build.md. The report cites it.

findings.what: held_over_bound and held_grew are now counted in every DelayStream test but asserted in only two. In the stalled-client test the asserts come before the drain phase, so the final woken write_all is never checked against the bound.
findings.fix: Follow-up for STATUS or the card, not this change-set: assert both counts again before drop(ds) at :842, and later in a shared helper used by every DelayStream test.

findings.where: spikes/netcode-proof/crates/net/src/l2/delay_tests.rs:2272 ("A few seconds"), :38 (HANG = 30 s); .gate/u3c-held-1/e3a.log ("finished in 15.70s" in 459 of 600 runs)
findings.what: Wording nit. G-NC2's rewritten doc keeps "A few seconds", but the test takes 15.67-15.72 s in all 600 E3a runs, about half its 30 s hang guard. The fix does not move the loop's exit: held bytes grow only at writes, so the first sample above 64 KB always follows a write above 64 KB.
findings.fix: Follow-up wording only, since C1 fixed this text exactly: "about 16 s (half the hang guard)".
